questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Advanced Kubernetes engineers translate theory into concrete, scalable designs with real-world DR and upgrade considerations.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet, PVCs, and StorageClass
- Anti-affinity and PodDisruptionBudget
- Readiness/Liveness probes and rolling updates
- Etcd backup/DR and cross-AZ failover testing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  serviceName: "example"
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app:latest
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you verify DR readiness after deployment?
- What changes to cluster autoscaler or etcd backup cadence would you consider for larger clusters?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design zero‑downtime credential rotation using in‑pod hot reload, a common real‑world constraint in production clusters.

## Key Concepts
- Secrets mounted as files
- Sidecar pattern for in‑place reload
- Process signaling (SIGHUP) or in‑app reload endpoint
- Rolling updates and canary validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Pod spec snippet (simplified)
containers:
  - name: app
    image: myapp:latest
  - name: cert-watcher
    image: alpine:3.18
    command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache inotify-tools; while inotifywait -e modify /etc/tls/secret; do kill -HUP 1; done"]
    volumeMounts:
      - name: tls
        mountPath: /etc/tls
```

- How would you test this under high traffic with a canary rollout?
- What failure modes exist (e.g., client handshake during reload) and mitigations?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical mastery of deployment strategies in large Kubernetes environments, emphasizing real-world constraints, traffic control, observability, and DR.

## Key Concepts
- Canary and blue/green deployments
- Traffic shaping with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd)
- Readiness/Liveness probes, PodDisruptionBudget
- Rollbacks, error budgets, observability
- DR planning, RBAC

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 25%
      maxSurge: 25%
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payments
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: myrepo/payments:canary-1
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you measure canary success and trigger rollback?
- What metrics and alerting would you configure?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests RBAC basics and real-world troubleshooting of startup-time configuration. Candidates must connect kubectl checks to a concrete fix, ensuring least privilege and minimal disruption.

## Key Concepts

- RBAC: Roles, RoleBindings, ServiceAccounts
- ConfigMaps and startup config loading
- kubectl auth can-i, jsonpath
- Rolling out a fix with a deployment rollout

## Code Example

```bash
# Identify SA for a pod
kubectl get pod <pod-name> -n <ns> -o jsonpath='{.spec.serviceAccountName}'

# Check access as that SA
kubectl auth can-i get configmaps -n <ns> --as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>

# If denied, create Role and RoleBinding
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: <ns>
  name: cm-read
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: cm-read-binding
  namespace: <ns>
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: <sa>
  namespace: <ns>
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: cm-read
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
EOF

# Redeploy to pick up new permissions
kubectl rollout restart deployment <deploy-name> -n <ns>

# Verify startup uses updated ConfigMap
kubectl logs -l app=<app-label> -n <ns> | tail -n 20
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you audit RBAC across the cluster for least privilege?
- What tests verify the fix persists after ConfigMap changes?
